column3: because the NAT hooks install a NAT null

column1: binding in case the iptables nat table (iptable_nat hooks) or the
corresponding nftables chain (nft nat hooks) doesn't specify a nat
transformation.
Null bindings are needed to detect port collsisions between NAT-ed and
non-NAT-ed connections.
This causes nftables NAT rules to not work when iptable_nat module is
loaded
column2: and vice versa because nat binding has already been attached

column1: when the second nat hook is consulted.
The netfilter core is not really the correct location to handle this
(hooks are just hooks
column2: the core has no notion of what kinds of side

column1: effects a hook implements)
column2: but its the only place where we can check

column1: for conflicts between both iptables hooks and nftables hooks without
adding dependencies.
So add nat annotation to hook_ops to describe those hooks that will
add NAT bindings and then make core reject if such a hook already exists.
The annotation fills a padding hole
we might change this to a 'u8 type' instead of bool.
